notes:
I hit the research tool's usage limit before I could read everything, so these notes have gaps. I wasn't able to read the full Gill, Ellicott or Pulpit chapter pages, or anything from oca.org, the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org), ag.org or wesley.nnu.edu. Everything below comes only from the pages I actually read. Some Biblehub excerpts and one Precept Austin note gave no author's name, and I've marked those as unnamed instead of guessing who wrote them.

---

## 1. Traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 1:** The disciples had good reason to be upset. They had just heard about a traitor, about denials and that Jesus was leaving. Guzik says Jesus doesn't promise a life without trouble, but he does promise an untroubled heart within it. Following Tenney, he reads the command as "stop being troubled." Following Alford and Morris, he takes both "believe"s as commands. Asking them to trust Jesus just as they trust God is, he says, a radical claim. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- The bible.org notes say the grammar means "stop letting your hearts be troubled." They point out that "hearts" is plural, so Jesus is speaking to all eleven, and that in Hebrew "heart" means the whole person. https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14
- MacArthur (quoted on Precept Austin) says Jesus was not calling them to saving faith, because they already had it. He was calling them to keep that same trust once he was no longer visibly with them. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- The NET notes say this is the same verb used of Jesus' own distress in 11:33, 12:27 and 13:21. Each "believe" could be a statement or a command, and the first could even be a question. https://classic.net.bible.org/passage.php/o/w/passage.php?passage=joh+14%3A1-4

**v. 2:** For Guzik, "my Father's house" means heaven, and "many rooms" means there is room for everyone. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- Gangel says the point is space, not large buildings: "there's room for you." Wiersbe criticises songs that promise mansions for faithful Christians and shacks for worldly ones. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/64252/
- Precept Austin says "prepare a place" refers to Jesus' death. Heaven isn't still being built. The place is ready now. Constable agrees: the place already existed, and Jesus' going is itself the preparation. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary ; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/john-14.html
- The Sermon Bible Commentary says Jesus links heaven with the idea of permanence. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/sbc/john-14.html

**v. 3:** Guzik says heaven is heaven because Jesus is there, not because of golden streets. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- The bible.org notes say the verb means "welcome a person," so heaven is personal fellowship with God. They add that the New Testament doesn't say exactly when that full fellowship begins. https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14
- Constable notes that John speaks of several "comings": after the resurrection, through the Spirit, and the final bodily return. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/john-14.html

**v. 4:** The NET notes say that for Jesus the way back to the Father went through the cross. For the disciples, the "way" is Jesus himself. https://classic.net.bible.org/passage.php/o/w/passage.php?passage=joh+14%3A1-4

**v. 6:** Guzik says Jesus doesn't claim to show or teach the way. He claims to be the way, and the claim is exclusive. If it's false, Guzik argues, Jesus was neither honest nor a true prophet. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- Leon Morris (on Precept Austin) says "way" is the link between God and sinners, "truth" is Jesus' complete reliability, and "life" means more than physical existence. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- Ryle says sincerity and earnestness can't save anyone without Christ. He calls the idea that every sincere person is saved by his own religion "a deadly and ruinous error." https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary-j-c-ryle
- Constable says Jesus doesn't only show the way, he is the way, because he redeems us. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/john-14.html
- The NET notes give an alternative translation: "the way, even the truth and the life." https://classic.net.bible.org/verse.php?book=Joh&chapter=14&verse=6

**v. 7:** Guzik says Jesus is the only way to God because he perfectly represents God. To know him is to know God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/

**v. 9:** For Guzik, seeing Jesus' love and actions is seeing the Father's. He says this ends the idea that the Old Testament God is cruel and Jesus is a kinder one, and points to Exodus 34. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/

**vv. 10–11:** Vincent (on Precept Austin) says Jesus answers Philip's doubt in two ways. His words come from the Father, and his works are the Father's works. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- The NET notes say both words and works reveal who Jesus is, but the works carry more weight as proof. "Works" most likely means the miraculous signs, which were a secondary basis for faith after the disciples' personal relationship with him. https://classic.net.bible.org/bible.php?book=Joh&chapter=14

**v. 12:** Guzik reads "greater" as greater in scope and size, not more spectacular. The Spirit, who came because Jesus went to the Father, would make this possible. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- A bible.org sermon says the 3,000 converted at Pentecost probably outnumber everyone converted during Jesus' ministry. It quotes Ryle: no work is greater than converting a soul. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-76-doing-greater-works-jesus-john-1412-14
- Ryle himself says Christ lets his weak servants have more success than he had in person. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary-j-c-ryle
- Several unnamed older commentators on Biblehub agree that the greater works are the whole work of the Church and the spread to the Gentiles, "not greater in nature and kind, but more in number." Vincent quotes Godet: Jesus' ministry in the flesh had to be local. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/14-12.htm

**vv. 13–14:** Calvin says Jesus is declaring himself the author of everything the apostles will do. He reads v. 14 as a deliberate repeat for people who feel unworthy to approach God. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-13.html ; https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-14.html
- Barnes says "in my name" means "for my sake," like drawing on someone's bank account with his permission. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-13.html
- Gill says it means pleading Christ's merits, and that the request must fit God's will and our real good. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-14.html
- Constable says the condition is not just adding "in Jesus' name" at the end. Drawing on 1 John 5:14–15, he says it means "according to God's will." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-14.html
- An unnamed older note on Biblehub says it means asking as Christ's representatives. It adds that prayers made in ignorance may be answered best by not being granted. https://biblehub.com/john/14-13.htm
- The bible.org notes say this is the only verse in John where Jesus tells people to pray to him. https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14

**v. 15:** The NET notes say this verse links the prayer promises to the promise of the Spirit, and that obedience proves real love. https://classic.net.bible.org/passage.php/o/w/passage.php?passage=Joh+14:15-24
- Ray Stedman (on Precept Austin) says love makes obedience easy. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john_commentaries_3

**vv. 16–17:** Guzik says "another" means another of the same kind, so the Spirit shows Jesus' own nature. The disciples would end up with more help, not less. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- The Sermon Bible Commentary says the Spirit is a permanent resident, not a passing visitor. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/sbc/john-14.html
- The bible.org notes say "Spirit of truth" is the opposite of Satan, the father of lies, and quote G. Campbell Morgan calling the Spirit "the other Jesus." https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14

**v. 18:** Guzik uses the orphan picture to list what the Spirit does: he shows that Jesus is alive, provides, teaches and protects. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- The NET notes say "orphans" may mean "helpless," and that "I will come" here mainly means the post-resurrection appearances. https://classic.net.bible.org/bible.php?book=Joh&chapter=14

**v. 19:** Ryle says Christ's resurrection guarantees his people's resurrection. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary-j-c-ryle
- Guzik says the disciples would "see" him in a fuller way than with their eyes. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/

**v. 20:** The NET notes say "that day" is better read as the resurrection appearances than as the second coming, because v. 19 says the world won't see him. https://classic.net.bible.org/bible.php?book=Joh&chapter=14

**v. 21:** Ryle says keeping Christ's commandments is the best test of loving him, and that good feelings without action are useless. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary-j-c-ryle
- The bible.org notes call obedience the evidence of true conversion. https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14

**v. 22:** The bible.org notes identify this Judas with Thaddaeus. https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14
- Precept Austin says Jesus answers by explaining that the Spirit will reveal him to genuine, obedient followers. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary

**v. 23:** Constable says Jesus doesn't correct Judas. He keeps the focus on loving obedience, which leads to close fellowship after Pentecost. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/john-14.html
- The NET notes say the indwelling here is individual rather than corporate. https://classic.net.bible.org/passage.php/o/w/passage.php?passage=Joh+14:15-24
- Guzik says this is not mainly a mystical or ecstatic experience. It is ordinary life lived in the Spirit. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/

**v. 24:** Constable reads this as v. 15 put negatively. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/john-14.html
- The bible.org notes ask whether "you" means the world or the disciples. https://bible.org/seriespage/john-14

**v. 26:** Guzik says the Spirit carries on the teaching Jesus began as a rabbi, and his work will look like Jesus' character as shown in Scripture. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- Tenney (on Precept Austin) says the Spirit teaches from within and brings Jesus' words back to mind, which prompts obedience. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary

**v. 27:** "Peace" (shalom) was a normal farewell. Guzik says Jesus gives the real peace of his own heart. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- Lenski describes the peace as a legacy and a treasure. Tenney says Jesus' peace comes from being sure of the Father's love, while the world's peace comes from ignoring danger or relying on oneself. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- Ryle says Christ gives peace freely and forever. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary-j-c-ryle
- The NET notes link the peace to the Spirit living in believers, and to Jesus' "peace" greetings in John 20. https://classic.net.bible.org/bible.php?book=Joh&chapter=14

**v. 28:** Precept Austin says the disciples should have rejoiced, because Jesus' glorification would bring the Spirit and the greater works. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- Constable compares it to grieving a believing friend who has died: we mourn our loss, but should rejoice more that they are with the Lord. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/john-14.html
- How "greater" should be understood is covered in section 3.

**v. 30:** The NET notes say "ruler of this world" means Satan, and give the Greek as "in me he has nothing." https://classic.net.bible.org/verse.php?book=Joh&chapter=14&verse=30
- Ryle says Satan found weakness in Adam and every saint, but "nothing" at all in Christ. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary-j-c-ryle

**v. 31:** Gangel (on Precept Austin) notes that 18:1 doesn't seem to match "let us go." Some think chapters 15–17 were spoken on the way. Others suspect the text has been rearranged. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary

I found nothing specific for vv. 5, 8, 25 or 29.

---

## 2. Where Protestant traditions differ

**v. 12 (continuationist vs. evangelism reading):** Sam Storms, a charismatic writer, rejects the popular "more souls saved" reading. He says the works are greater because they happen in the age of the Spirit, after the cross. He holds that these works are "not less than" miracles and healings. https://www.samstorms.org/enjoying-god-blog/post/what-are-the--greater-works--in-john-1412-and-who-performs-them-and-when
- Guzik pushes back on people who think individual believers should do more spectacular miracles than Jesus did. He says he is still waiting for proof. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-14/
- The bible.org sermon says no one today does miracles equal to Christ's, but allows that the Spirit sometimes works in unusual ways. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-76-doing-greater-works-jesus-john-1412-14

**vv. 13–14 (labelled by tradition on StudyLight):** Adam Clarke (Wesleyan) applies the promise to working miracles and converting souls. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-13.html
- Gill (Baptist, Calvinist) says Christ is equally to be prayed to as the Father. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-14.html
- Chuck Smith (Calvary Chapel) says the promise is for disciples who have surrendered to the Father's will. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/14-13.html

**v. 26 (does the Spirit give new revelation?):** Spurgeon says the Spirit reveals nothing new today, the canon is closed, and claims of fresh revelation are "generally revealed nonsense." https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- I found no charismatic response to this.

**v. 3 (rapture):** Wiersbe calls the verse a clear promise of Christ's return, citing 1 Thessalonians 4. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/64252/
- Precept Austin lists a Mike Vlach sermon on John 14:1–3 as evidence for a pre-tribulation rapture. I only saw the title. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john_commentaries
- The NET notes read v. 3 as both the second coming and the resurrection appearances. https://classic.net.bible.org/bible.php?book=Joh&chapter=18

---

## 3. Other views

**v. 2 (scholarship):** The NET notes report that many link the word for "rooms" to an Aramaic word for a traveller's rest stop. Origen took it as stages on the road to God. The NET prefers "permanent dwelling" and praises Luther's translation *Wohnungen*. Since John 2:16 uses "my Father's house" for the temple, they suggest the dwelling place may ultimately be "in" Jesus himself. https://classic.net.bible.org/verse.php?book=Joh&chapter=14&verse=2 ; https://classic.net.bible.org/passage.php/o/w/passage.php?passage=joh+14%3A1-4

**v. 12 (Catholic):** A Catholic Answers homily says our cooperation with God in saving souls is a greater work than Christ's miracles. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/online-edition/greater-works-than-these

**vv. 13–14 (popular misuse):** GotQuestions says treating "in Jesus' name" as a magic formula that guarantees an answer is unbiblical. https://www.gotquestions.org/pray-Jesus-name.html
- I found no page that named or described prosperity or word-of-faith teaching on this verse directly.

**v. 28 (the Father "greater"):** Augustine says Jesus is less than the Father only in his human "servant-form," and equal in his divine nature. He answers the Arians directly. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701078.htm
- The Gospel Coalition quotes Augustine to the same effect. https://ca.thegospelcoalition.org/columns/detrinitate/is-the-father-greater-than-the-son/
- Catholic Answers says the Father holds higher rank as Father and as the one who sent Jesus, and that this doesn't deny Jesus' divinity. https://www.catholic.com/audio/ddp/the-father-is-greater-than-i
- An unnamed note on Precept Austin says the Father is greater in office, not in nature. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-14-commentary
- An unnamed older commentator on Biblehub says the verse has been argued over in every age. He thinks the "human nature only" explanation is "not here thought of." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/14-28.htm

**Orthodox:** I found nothing, because I couldn't reach oca.org.
